## North Georgia Soil Dynamics & Engineering Practices
A primary differentiator for AGS Stones is site engineering for Georgia Piedmont Red Clay:
- Soil Characteristics: Georgia red clay has high plasticity index, expanding significantly when saturated and contracting into hard fissures during hot summer dry spells.
- Poured Concrete Problem: Rigid slabs lack flexibility. Soil expansion exerts uneven uplift, causing premature cracking along stress planes.
- Paver Solution: Interlocking concrete pavers sit on an aggregate base (typically 6 inches for patios, 8 to 12 inches of compacted crusher run for driveways) separated from subgrade clay by heavy-duty non-woven geotextile fabric. The flexible joints filled with stabilized polymeric sand allow micro-movement without surface cracking.
- Retaining Wall Hydrostatic Relief: Retaining walls fail primarily due to trapped water weight (hydrostatic pressure). AGS Stones installs clean washed #57 gravel backfill extending 12 inches behind the block face, combined with 4-inch perforated PVC drain pipes wrapped in filter fabric and daylighted downhill to prevent water buildup.

## Hardscape Regulations & Permitting Quick Reference
- Retaining Walls: International Residential Code (IRC) Section R404.4. Walls under 4 feet of exposed height rarely require building permits or engineered drawings. Walls 4 feet or higher require calculations stamped by a Georgia Professional Engineer (PE). Surcharge loads (supporting driveways or structures) require engineering regardless of height.
- Impervious Surface Caps: Sandy Springs, Alpharetta, and Johns Creek limit lot coverage (typically 30% to 50%). Permeable Interlocking Concrete Paver (PICP) systems qualify as pervious surface in most municipalities.
- Georgia Drainage Law: Civil Law Rule of Surface Waters prohibits artificially concentrating or directing runoff onto neighboring properties.
- HOA Requirements: Most North Atlanta HOAs require Architectural Review Committee (ARC) packages containing scaled site plans, manufacturer material cut sheets, drainage arrows, and contractor certificates of insurance.
